title: Courtesy on a Date
short: Be on time, put the phone away, listen, be kind to staff, and settle who pays ahead; customs range from the inviter paying to splitting, and both are polite.
trouble: Learners assume there is one rule about who pays. Writers disagree; what matters is that it is settled without pressure or awkwardness.

blocks.html: Once a plan is made and accepted, a date is a chance to get to know someone. The courtesies are the ones you already know from restaurants, phones and conversation. One question, who pays, comes back from splitting the bill.
Be on time, put the phone away, listen, and be kind to staff. Settle who pays ahead: customs range from the inviter paying to splitting, and both are polite.

Being on time and putting the phone away say "you matter to me tonight." Listening is how two people get to know each other. Kindness to servers and staff shows how a person treats everyone, which is worth knowing. Who pays is a matter where writers disagree, so the courteous thing is to settle it early and without pressure, so the meal can be about the company.

head: Who pays: common customs
What makes it polite
rows: It is offered as a treat, without strings
Both are comfortable with the plan
Offered sincerely, and the answer is accepted
blocks.cap: Customs vary, and writers disagree. Each is polite when both agree.

blocks.title: The check arrives
blocks.q: Ruby invited Kofi to dinner. The check arrives, and neither has mentioned paying. What would make it easy?
steps: By the old custom, the one who invited pays, and Ruby can simply take the check.
Kofi may offer to split; if Ruby says "My treat," he thanks her warmly.
Better still: settle it when making the plan.
blocks.a: Settle it early; either way, accept graciously.

blocks.title: Phones at the table
blocks.q: On a first date, Nora's phone buzzes during dinner. What should she do?
steps: She leaves it silenced and out of sight.
If she is waiting for something important, she says so at the start and steps away if needed.
blocks.a: Leave it away, or mention a needed call at the start.

cards.why: Kindness to staff shows how you treat everyone.
Put it away; the person in front of you comes first.

cards.text: Agreeing ahead of time how you will pay
Arguing over the check at the table

blocks.html: Assuming there is one rule about who pays. Writers disagree; what matters is that it is settled without pressure or awkwardness. Quick check: did you both agree, or did one of you just assume?
